messages:
morgan: quick check-in on the adaptor follow-up — want to nail the backpressure & veto protocol before we expand canary. thoughts?

jia: main risk is adaptor-driven churn when residency keeps vetoing. we should formalize a backoff contract.

devon: agree. propose ephemeral veto counters per-prefix. adaptor sees `onVeto` with a count and must respect exponential backoff.

morgan: good. add max_retries and a cooldown window. also need a hint update so adaptors lower aggression.

rachel: telemetry: emit `evict.veto` with reason and consecutive_veto_count. ops needs to graph it.

kevin: another angle — backpressure at node-level. if residency is saturated, adaptors should get a `NodePressure` signal and reduce eviction attempts globally.

anjali: NodePressure sounds right. how do adaptors subscribe? poll in backgroundTick or push via a small shared ring?

jia: lightweight push via a in-memory atomic flag is fine. adaptors check a `node_pressure_level` in evaluate() params. keep it cheap.

devon: correctness table: evaluate can return {keep, demote_hint, evict_request, preempt_score}. residency validates evict_request w/fast checks (pinned/inflight). if veto -> returns veto code.

morgan: callout: residency veto must be O(1) and lock-free if possible. otherwise hot path suffers.

kevin: implement veto fast checks using per-prefix atomic bitset: pinned|inflight|recently_demoted. single load is enough.

rachel: also add `decision_id` to trace decisions through logs: adaptor + residency + final action. helps correlate.

anjali: how about cross-prefix fairness? adaptors making local decisions can starve other prefixes. we need a `node_budget` token API.

jia: token API idea: adaptor calls `ReserveTokens(n)` and residency grants up to available. tokens consumed per-evict. if none, adaptor should back off.

devon: token lease should be short (like 250ms) to avoid hoarding. and lease return on veto.

kevin: corner case: adaptor calls evaluate for many prefixes > budget. we must ensure evaluate stays O(1). So reserveTokens should be a separate cheap check, not blocking.

morgan: agree. evaluate gets a `budget_hint` showing approximate available tokens. adaptor uses it to decide to request evict or schedule for later.

rachel: integration tests: 1) adaptor suggests evict, residency vetoes, token returned; 2) under NodePressure node denies reserves; 3) fairness stress with mixed tenant sizes.

anjali: perf: prefer compiled adaptors on-path. sidecar scoring service can compute heavy signals and write hints to shared memory.

jia: we can expose a `hint` bag: small struct of ints (hot_score, last_seen_window, tenant_pressure) that adaptor evaluate uses. sidecar updates hints. keep bag <= 64 bytes.

devon: suggestion: avoid WASM for now on hot path. we can later prototype WASM with JIT warm paths.

kevin: timeouts: evaluate must return within 3ms, else residency treats as error and uses fallback legacy decision. emit `evict.adaptor_timeout`.

morgan: rollout plan tweak: expand canary only if `evict.veto_ratio < 5%` and `evict.adaptor_timeouts=0` for 1h.

rachel: also watch downstream SLOs: p95 tokenization latency etc — eviction churn can indirectly affect those.

anjali: one more: make adaptor version immutable once active on node; config pushes create new versions to avoid mixing behavior mid-flight. residency should tag decisions with adaptor_version.

jia: and signal when adaptor_version changes so we can correlate regressions.

devon: docs: add a small section in runbook: backup rollback steps, metric queries, and safe thresholds for `evict.fallback_count` and `evict.veto_ratio`.

kevin: implementation owners: I'll own token API + NodePressure flag.

anjali: I'll build hint-bag sidecar and compiled adaptor glue.

jia: I'll wire metrics + canary gating.

rachel: I'll do tests and dashboards.

devon: I'll add e2e perf harness and the veto correctness tests.

morgan: infra-bot, schedule a canary expansion job (10->30 nodes) once owners mark tasks done. set alert on veto_ratio>5% or adaptor_timeouts>0.

infra-bot: Canary expansion scheduled. Alert rules: evict.veto_ratio > 5% OR evict.adaptor_timeouts > 0 OR node_pressure_level high for >2m.

morgan: thanks. last ask — make sure adaptors annotate their reason codes with short human strings so on-call can triage quickly.

rachel: will add `reason_text` label to evict.decisions.

kevin: one follow-up discussion item: fairness across nodes when a tenant spans multiple nodes. opened issue #EV-214 to track.

morgan: perfect. closing for now, re-open if any regressions during expansion. :white_check_mark:
